title: Proverbs Wisdom IQ
subtitle: Can you tell a real Proverb from a clever lookalike?

questions.text: Who is traditionally credited with most of the book of Proverbs?

options.explanation: Proverbs 1:1 opens with "The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel." Solomon is the figure most tied to the book.
Moses is connected with the first five books of the Bible, not the book of Proverbs.
David, Solomon's father, is mostly tied to the Psalms. Proverbs is credited largely to Solomon.
Paul wrote letters in the New Testament, long after Proverbs was written.

questions.text: Complete this well known Proverb: "Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, and ..."

options.explanation: Proverbs 3:5 (ASV) reads, "Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, and lean not upon thine own understanding."

options.text: "all your dreams will surely come true"
options.explanation: This sounds nice, but it is not in Proverbs. The verse calls us not to lean on our own understanding.
That is a modern saying, not the words of Proverbs 3:5.
This is a common motivational line, not Scripture. The real verse points us away from our own understanding.

questions.text: Which of these is an actual teaching found in the book of Proverbs?

options.explanation: This is a popular saying often mistaken for Scripture, but it is not in Proverbs or anywhere in the Bible.
Proverbs 15:1 (ASV) reads, "A soft answer turneth away wrath; but a grievous word stirreth up anger."
This is a modern phrase, not a Proverb. The genuine teaching speaks of a soft answer turning away wrath.
Proverbs actually warns about trusting our own hearts. This saying is not in the book.

questions.text: According to Proverbs, what is the beginning of knowledge?

options.explanation: Effort matters, but Proverbs points to something deeper as the starting place.
Proverbs 1:7 (ASV) reads, "The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge."
Schooling has value, yet Proverbs names the fear of Jehovah as the beginning of knowledge.
That is a modern idea, not the teaching of Proverbs, which points to the fear of Jehovah.

questions.text: Complete this Proverb: "Pride goeth before destruction, and ..."

options.explanation: Proverbs 16:18 (ASV) reads, "Pride goeth before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall."
That is not how the verse ends. It speaks of a haughty spirit before a fall.
This is a paraphrase at best. The actual line is about a haughty spirit before a fall.
Proverbs does talk about fools elsewhere, but this verse ends with a haughty spirit before a fall.

questions.text: Which saying is NOT from the book of Proverbs?

options.text: "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches"
options.explanation: This one is real. Proverbs 22:1 (ASV) reads, "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches."
This common proverb is not from the Bible. Scripture values honesty, but this exact saying is not in the book of Proverbs.

options.text: "He that spareth his rod hateth his son"
options.explanation: This is genuine. Proverbs 13:24 (ASV) begins, "He that spareth his rod hateth his son."

options.text: "A merry heart doeth good like a medicine"
options.explanation: This one is real too. Proverbs 17:22 (ASV) reads, "A cheerful heart is a good medicine," rendered in older wording as a merry heart doing good like a medicine.

questions.text: Proverbs urges the lazy person to learn from which small creature?

options.explanation: Proverbs 6:6 (ASV) reads, "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise."
Sparrows appear elsewhere in Scripture, but Proverbs points the sluggard to the ant.
The bee is a fine example of industry, yet the verse names the ant.
The spider is mentioned in Proverbs in another place, but the sluggard is told to consider the ant.

questions.text: What does Proverbs say about a friend's loyalty in hard times?

options.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 (ASV) reads, "A friend loveth at all times; and a brother is born for adversity."
Proverbs is more hopeful than that. It says a friend loves at all times.

options.text: "Keep your circle small and trust no one"
options.explanation: This is a modern saying, not Proverbs, which speaks of a friend who loves at all times.

options.text: "A friend is only as good as their last favor"
options.explanation: That cynical line is not in the book. Proverbs says a friend loves at all times.

questions.text: Complete this Proverb about raising children: "Train up a child in the way he should go, and ..."

options.text: "when he is old, he will not depart from it"
options.explanation: Proverbs 22:6 (ASV) reads, "Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it."

options.text: "he will make you proud one day"
options.explanation: That is not the verse. It says that when he is old he will not depart from it.

options.text: "he will choose his own path in time"
options.explanation: This is a modern sentiment, not the words of Proverbs 22:6.
The verse makes no such promise. It speaks of the child not departing from the way when he is old.

questions.text: How does Proverbs describe the path of the righteous?

options.text: Like a stormy sea that never settles
options.explanation: That is not the image used. Proverbs compares the righteous path to growing light.

options.text: Like the dawning light that shines brighter and brighter
options.explanation: Proverbs 4:18 (ASV) reads, "But the path of the righteous is as the dawning light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day."

options.text: Like a road that always stays the same
options.explanation: The picture is of growing brightness, not a road that never changes.

options.text: Like a candle that quickly burns out
options.explanation: Proverbs paints the opposite. The righteous path shines more and more unto the perfect day.

questions.text: Proverbs says, "A good name is rather to be chosen than ..." what?

options.explanation: Proverbs 22:1 (ASV) reads, "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favor rather than silver and gold."
The verse compares a good name to riches, not to length of days.
Friends are valued elsewhere, but this verse sets a good name above great riches.
The contrast in the verse is with great riches, not with rank or position.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the book of Proverbs?

options.text: To record the history of Israel's kings
options.explanation: History is told in other books. Proverbs is a book of wisdom for daily living.

options.text: To give wisdom and instruction for living well
options.explanation: Proverbs opens by stating it is written to know wisdom and instruction, and to guide people in living wisely.

options.text: To list the laws given at Mount Sinai
options.explanation: The Law is found in earlier books. Proverbs offers practical wisdom rather than the Sinai laws.

options.text: To predict events in the last days
options.explanation: Prophecy of the end appears in other books. Proverbs is focused on wisdom for everyday life.
